item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Anticonvulsant (N0415K1 Is taking; N0415K2 Indication noted)

lookback_source.quote: N0415K1. Anticonvulsant: Check if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back/observation period, or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. The item table on p. N-4 states the check is for medications taken "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days." The coding instructions on p. N-6 refer to a "7-day observation period" for Column 1; the subitem instructions on p. N-8 refer to a "7-day observation period" for N0415K1 and to "the observation period" for N0415K2. The document does not state how the days are counted relative to the ARD in this section.

coding_levels.label: Anticonvulsant — Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415K1. Anticonvulsant: Check if an anticonvulsant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Anticonvulsant — Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all anticonvulsant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415K2. Anticonvulsant: Check if there is an indication noted for all anticonvulsant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: None of the above
coding_levels.definition: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1 (N0415K1): check if the resident is taking an anticonvulsant by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (N0415K2): only if Column 1 is checked, check whether an indication is noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as an antianxiety medication).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the anticonvulsant medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received the medication while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., medication given in the emergency room) must be reviewed.

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: The indication must be an identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based on the prescriber's assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding of pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") with an expectation that the source can be identified.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415K (Anticonvulsant) to any payment or case-mix classification.
